messages.subject: Discussion on extracting-scanqtl-information-lod2p-value-skipping-missing-values
parts:
> Can somebody help me to extract information from scanqtl() for the highest LOD between >2 > loci with dimnames containing pseudomarker or marker information and the joint LOD?

You could do something like the following:

data(hyper)
hyper <- sim.geno(hyper, step=0, n.draws=20)
out <- scanqtl(hyper, chr=c(1,1,4), pos=list(c(-Inf,50),c(50,Inf),c(-
Inf,Inf)))
max.out <- max(out, na.rm=TRUE)
loc <- which(!is.na(out) & out==max.out, arr.ind=TRUE)
thenam <- loc
for(i in seq(along=loc))
thenam[i] <- dimnames(out)[[i]][loc[i]]

> Secondly, how can I translate LOD into a p-value?

LOD scores from scanqtl cannot easily be translated into p-values.

LOD scores from scanone can be translated by doing a permutation
test. See the "Tour of R/qtl" document at http://www.rqtl.org/tutorials/rqtltour.pdf
Particularly look at Example 1, item 15, on page 6.

> Thirdly, how can a extract a subset of individuals from a cross-object without missing data?

You can use subset.cross to extract a subset of individuals. For
example, consider the following.

data(listeria)
listeria.nomissing <- subset(listeria, ind = !is.na(listeria$pheno[,
1]))
